Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: S-Rolling: Steerable Rolling Gaits for Twistable Snake Robots in Low-Clearance Environments
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: The paper introduces S-rolling, a novel steerable rolling gait for snake robots that enables low-clearance maneuverability while maintaining a low swept height and efficient steering.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Snake robots can traverse complex environments with limbless locomotion, but maneuvering in low-clearance environments remains challenging because a gait must maintain a small swept height while also providing planar steering. Existing rolling gaits preserve a low swept height body configuration but generally provide limited steering, whereas steering gaits often introduce vertical undulation and require additional clearance. With that in mind, this paper develops S-rolling, a steerable rolling gait that combines low swept height locomotion with planar maneuverability for twistable snake robots. S-rolling is designed using an S-shaped planar backbone curve, whose head and tail segments roll with independently controlled angular velocities, producing different motion modes. We derive its joint space gait equation, in which a central twist joint realizes the relative rotation between the two segments. We also develop a quasi-static kinematic model relating the segment rolling speeds to the linear and angular velocities of the robot. Real-robot experiments demonstrate the various motion modes, traversal through a 10 cm clearance test track, and maneuvering tasks beneath a large workpiece and a car chassis. In these low-clearance scenarios, S-rolling successfully performs approximately 90$^\circ$ and 180$^\circ$ heading changes, whereas the baseline rolling arc gait cannot change the robot heading.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: This paper presents new linear twisting sidewinding gaits for snake robots, enhancing speed and reducing motor strain while improving locomotion on complex terrains.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. Yet its twisting is concentrated in a short buffer segment, imposing most of the workload on the two twist joints in the middle, which can often overburden the motors and limit its locomotion. With that in mind, this paper develops a new family of twisting sidewinding gaits that distribute the workload over the entire body with our proposed linear twisting function. Under matched turning speed and total output power, our gaits reduce the peak output power of a single twist joint by 42%. Real-robot experiments show that, with the reduced workload, our new gaits can locomote the robot in various terrains that the existing rolling vector approach cannot. Besides, our new gaits can move up to 49% faster than conventional sidewinding without twisting.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: AdvFidelity: Unifying Preference Alignment and Few-Step Image Generation within Reinforcement Learning
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Sicong Kang, Fangao Zeng, Yuhan Li, Hao Zhou, Mengfei Xu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: AdvFidelity unifies preference alignment and efficient few-step image generation in reinforcement learning by incorporating artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision through an online adversarial reward mechanism.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Practical image generation requires both human preference alignment and few-step efficiency, yet combining reinforcement learning (RL) with distillation is often multi-stage and may erode RL gains We observe that few-step RL progressively improves structural coherence, even with specialized rewards, but leaves low-level artifacts that these rewards may fail to penalize. To address this gap, we propose AdvFidelity, which integrates artifact-sensitive fidelity supervision into RL through an online adversarial reward. This enables joint reward alignment and high-fidelity few-step generation within a single RL stage, without distribution matching distillation (DMD) or other explicit distillation objectives. We train a discriminator to rank high-quality references (positives) above content-matched reconstructions (negatives) produced by the current generator. Reconstructing moderately noised references largely preserves style and scene layout while exposing low-level degradations. This encourages the discriminator to assess artifacts rather than content differences. With negatives reconstructed online, alternating updates adapt fidelity supervision to the generator's evolving failure modes. References can come from existing target-domain data or full-step model samples. Built on LeapAlign, AdvFidelity backpropagates gradients from both rewards through the few-step sampling trajectories used at inference. Across two model backbones and three task settings, AdvFidelity matches full-step LeapAlign in alignment, task performance, and overall generation quality and remains highly competitive with other evaluated full-step RL methods, using only 4 or 8 steps without CFG.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Yifan Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Xiaojun Ye, Yifei Liu, Donggang Li
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: SpatialBrain enhances spatial reasoning by integrating experience with scene observations, improving decision-making across benchmarks without altering its fixed vision-language backbone.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: DepState-JEPA introduces a dual-stream RGB-Depth architecture for robot manipulation, enhancing predictive state representation by integrating spatial understanding and action-conditioned predictions through shared latent states.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce \textbf{DepState-JEPA}, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, \textbf{DepState}. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Kaijun Zhou, Zhiyang Li, Le Chen, Jinyu Gu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: rMuscle introduces a dual-phase muscle-memory cache for Vision-Language-Action models, enhancing inference speed by 1.29-1.42X while preserving task success rates in robotic applications.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Factory work is a promising early scenario for embodied AI: assigning repetitive manual jobs to robots has clear economic payoff, and a structured station keeps the jobs tractable for current policies. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models now dominate as the policy paradigm for these robots. The inference latency of VLA models directly affects robot responsiveness and motion smoothness. However, existing VLA inference frameworks do not fully exploit the characteristics of embodied workloads or account for the distinct bottlenecks across different stages of VLA inference. In this paper, we first characterize embodied workloads and identify substantial task similarity across repeated robot executions. We further find that such similarity extends beyond observations and action trajectories to internal model states. Drawing on these observations, we present rMuscle, a real-time VLA inference framework inspired by human muscle memory. It exploits cross-execution similarity through a dual-phase muscle-memory cache. The Context Cache reuses visual-token outputs to reduce computation, while the Action Cache reuses neuron activation patterns to reduce weight accesses. We keep both the cache memory footprint and access overhead low through online cache recomputation, sliding-window cache retrieval, and mask sharing across consecutive denoising steps. rMuscle achieves 1.29-1.42X speedup on RTX 4090 and Jetson Thor across LIBERO, RoboTwin, and physical manipulation tasks, while maintaining the original success rates on real-world robots.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Robot Learning with Visual Predicted Force
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Haonan Chen, Feiyang Wu, Yuxiang Ma, Mustafa Mete, Pengfei Ye
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: This paper presents a method for force-aware manipulation using visual force prediction from a compliant gripper, eliminating the need for specialized force sensors during deployment.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Force-aware manipulation typically relies on specialized force or tactile sensors. We show that force-aware manipulation can instead be achieved through visual force prediction from the deformation of a compliant Fin Ray gripper. Our approach trains two models. First, we train a visual force estimator on calibration data and use it to annotate task demonstrations with force estimates. Second, we train an action--force proposal policy on these force-augmented demonstrations to jointly generate candidate robot actions and their associated forces. At test time, we sample candidate actions and the forces they are expected to produce, then execute the action whose predicted force is closest to a target from the demonstrations. We evaluate our approach on berry picking, empty-can grasping, in-hand reorientation, and plug insertion. Our results show that visual force prediction can guide inference-time action selection for contact-rich manipulation without requiring force or tactile sensors at deployment.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Ruotong Liao, Meikel Kokowski, Xiaoxiao Sun, Yongqin Xian, Laura Bravo Sánchez
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: ProactEgoMem introduces a benchmark for evaluating proactive memory in streaming egocentric video, focusing on tasks like information capture, state tracking, and location tracking.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. Doing so on the user's behalf requires identifying what matters, understanding the scene in real time, and initiating memory maintenance in the background while the user stays focused on their activities. We introduce ProactEgoMem, a benchmark that evaluates proactive memory in streaming egocentric video. Three tasks ground the evaluation in ambient environmental needs: Information Capture (IC) preserves transient yet dense visual information, State Tracking (ST) follows changing object states, and Location Tracking (LT) records object movements. The benchmark defines its protocol at two levels of proactiveness: the Notification Level asks for a single timely notification that satisfies the user's intent, while the deeper Intervention Level asks the agent to maintain memory on the user's behalf through an active start-to-stop tool lifecycle. Parallel ProactEgoMem-Daily and ProactEgoMem-Sci tracks contain 300/100 clips covering daily and scientific use cases, paired with 1000/500 questions in ProactEgoMem-QA, which measures the quality of the proactively acquired memory. Across proprietary, open-source, video-language, and streaming baselines, even the strongest models fail to capture memory both timely and accurately. ProactEgoMem provides a rigorous evaluation foundation for proactive multimodal assistance and for video agents that co-exist with their users.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Guillem Casadesus Vila, Sri Aditya Deevi, Grace X. Gao
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: This study evaluates the transferability of Earth-trained humanoid locomotion controllers to lunar conditions, revealing asymmetric survival rates and the impact of terrain and gravity on performance.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. Learned locomotion has studied reduced gravity on rigid ground and granular terrain mostly at Earth gravity, but not humanoids under both, generalist-controller transfer, or the Earth cost of lunar adaptation. On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity on three held-out soil models. We also test the frozen SONIC, a released generalist humanoid controller, at both gravities on rigid ground only. Gravity transfer is asymmetric. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground, Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth, and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon. Rough training lifts combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon. In 3D RFT, soil training helps on Earth sand, on tiles and for rough-trained policies also on flat sand. On the stiffer lunar soil it helps only flat-trained Earth policies at Earth and changes the survival of Moon-trained policies by at most a few hundredths. In the sampled rollouts of the held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith at the low G1 foot pressure, with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39 apart from one seed with a short rigid reference. A gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain has a seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees. Lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: FoveaVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by utilizing learned foveation actions to replace wrist cameras, improving manipulation success rates in various tasks.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Wrist cameras provide close-up detail but restrict the view to the end-effector's surroundings. External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Yash Rampuria, Rohan Garg, Daniele Gammelli, Marco Pavone
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: GGraph is a GPU-accelerated library that enhances graph-based robot deployment and learning, enabling efficient training across hundreds of parallel environments.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Autonomous mobile robots require spatial representations that capture geometry and semantics while staying sparse enough for planning in large, unknown environments. Graphs provide a natural representation for this purpose and underpin both classical planning methods and a growing class of reinforcement-learning (RL) policies. However, RL training needs hundreds to thousands of parallel environments, each constructing and updating its own graph. Existing graph libraries are typically designed for either single-robot deployment or fixed graphs, and CPU-based graph construction limits scalable training to only a few dozen environments. We introduce GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning. GGraph supports real robots through ROS 2 interfaces and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks including 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration. For single-robot operation, GGraph updates graphs in milliseconds. At scale, it enables graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude. Across simulation and real-world experiments, these results establish GGraph as a unified graph infrastructure for both large-scale robot learning and deployment.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Matthew Strong, Ankush K. Dhawan, Julien Poffet, Giuse Pham, Jinho So
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R) transforms a single human RGB video into thousands of robot demonstrations by semantically aligning objects, enhancing robot learning efficiency.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Hyunji Alex Nam, Michael Dennis, Natasha Jaques, Minsuk Chang
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The paper presents TURTLE, an unsupervised approach for evolving scalable, self-tuning benchmarks to enhance AI tool-use capabilities across diverse applications.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $τ$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: SSIO: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Yuheng Qiu, Yutian Chen, Carlton Cort, Weison Huang, Shibo Zhao
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The SSIO method enables training inertial odometry models without ground-truth trajectories by using integration self-supervision and pose graph distillation, achieving high accuracy across diverse platforms.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Learning inertial odometry for a new platform usually requires ground-truth trajectories. We show that an inertial odometry model can instead be trained from scratch by a myopic teacher that integrates the IMU over each short window independently, a scheme we call integration self-supervision. Interestingly, although supervised only by short-window velocity changes, the student learns to directly predict velocity, and does so more accurately than its integration teacher. Pose graph distillation then refines the model with sequence-consistent targets from a pose graph over many windows. Training on a new platform therefore no longer requires collecting ground-truth trajectories, but only calibrating the IMU and recording data during normal operation. Across six datasets spanning pedestrians, drones, quadrupeds, and a humanoid, the same recipe with no velocity or position labels trains models that come within 0.07~m/s average velocity error of a same-architecture supervised baseline.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: FallGown: A Soft Pneumatic Wearable Device for Fall Prevention
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Megan C. Coram, Haoran Lei, Steven H. Collins, Steve B. Cousins, Michelle Baldonado
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The FallGown is a lightweight, soft pneumatic wearable device designed to prevent falls in older adults, offering support and adaptability while minimizing user burden.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Concerns about falling and potential resulting injuries prevent many older adults from participating in forms of health-improving exercise such as walking, dance, and tai chi. Existing passive devices like walkers require use of the arms for support, and active devices like exoskeletons and robotic frames are often rigid, bulky, and stigmatized, which limits their use. The FallGown is a soft wearable support structure consisting of pressurized pneumatic pouches within a fabric shell; it can support the full weight of a user's body and aims to prevent falls. It is portable (6.9 kg and 0.051 m3 when stored), minimally burdensome (7.24-20.8 N drag force depending on floor type and whether an optional rolling base frame is used), and convenient (less than 2.5 minutes on average to don and less than 0.5 minutes on average to doff). The optional rolling base lowers friction with the floor, but reduces portability and skirt deformation (which can be useful to fit through doors and other tight spaces). Fall prevention testing with a single user revealed a tradeoff between device size and stability against tipping; a skirt with 12 pneumatic pouches and a floor diameter of 1.4 meters with a base frame prevented all falls except in one case with a mechanical failure. On-board pressure sensors can sense the user's weight distribution, providing an opportunity for monitored exercise and adaptive support.

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Yash Rampuria, Rohan Garg, Daniele Gammelli, Marco Pavone

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Matthew Strong, Ankush K. Dhawan, Julien Poffet, Giuse Pham, Jinho So
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).summary: Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R) transforms a single human RGB video into thousands of robot demonstrations by semantically aligning objects, enhancing robot learning efficiency.
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).debug_abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Hyunji Alex Nam, Michael Dennis, Natasha Jaques, Minsuk Chang
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).summary: The paper presents TURTLE, an unsupervised approach for evolving scalable, self-tuning benchmarks to enhance AI tool-use capabilities across diverse applications.
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).debug_abstract: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $τ$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).title: SSIO: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Yuheng Qiu, Yutian Chen, Carlton Cort, Weison Huang, Shibo Zhao
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).summary: The SSIO method enables training inertial odometry models without ground-truth trajectories by using integration self-supervision and pose graph distillation, achieving high accuracy across diverse platforms.
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).debug_abstract: Learning inertial odometry for a new platform usually requires ground-truth trajectories. We show that an inertial odometry model can instead be trained from scratch by a myopic teacher that integrates the IMU over each short window independently, a scheme we call integration self-supervision. Interestingly, although supervised only by short-window velocity changes, the student learns to directly predict velocity, and does so more accurately than its integration teacher. Pose graph distillation then refines the model with sequence-consistent targets from a pose graph over many windows. Training on a new platform therefore no longer requires collecting ground-truth trajectories, but only calibrating the IMU and recording data during normal operation. Across six datasets spanning pedestrians, drones, quadrupeds, and a humanoid, the same recipe with no velocity or position labels trains models that come within 0.07~m/s average velocity error of a same-architecture supervised baseline.

Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).title: FallGown: A Soft Pneumatic Wearable Device for Fall Prevention
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).authors_text: Megan C. Coram, Haoran Lei, Steven H. Collins, Steve B. Cousins, Michelle Baldonado
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).summary: The FallGown is a lightweight, soft pneumatic wearable device designed to prevent falls in older adults, offering support and adaptability while minimizing user burden.
Stanford AI Lab (SAIL).debug_abstract: Concerns about falling and potential resulting injuries prevent many older adults from participating in forms of health-improving exercise such as walking, dance, and tai chi. Existing passive devices like walkers require use of the arms for support, and active devices like exoskeletons and robotic frames are often rigid, bulky, and stigmatized, which limits their use. The FallGown is a soft wearable support structure consisting of pressurized pneumatic pouches within a fabric shell; it can support the full weight of a user's body and aims to prevent falls. It is portable (6.9 kg and 0.051 m3 when stored), minimally burdensome (7.24-20.8 N drag force depending on floor type and whether an optional rolling base frame is used), and convenient (less than 2.5 minutes on average to don and less than 0.5 minutes on average to doff). The optional rolling base lowers friction with the floor, but reduces portability and skirt deformation (which can be useful to fit through doors and other tight spaces). Fall prevention testing with a single user revealed a tradeoff between device size and stability against tipping; a skirt with 12 pneumatic pouches and a floor diameter of 1.4 meters with a base frame prevented all falls except in one case with a mechanical failure. On-board pressure sensors can sense the user's weight distribution, providing an opportunity for monitored exercise and adaptive support.

通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).debug_abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. 通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).title: Minimal Witness Reinforcement Learning
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).authors_text: T. Y. Tsui, Zihao Ye, Pengxiang Cai, Yanchao Li, Yuqiang Li
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).summary: Minimal-Witness Reinforcement Learning (MWRL) identifies multiple minimal sufficient witnesses in RL by crediting proposals based on their contribution to the overall solution set.
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).debug_abstract: ``What are the irreducible conditions that are sufficient to produce an outcome?'' is one of the most common questions that recur across computation and science. Its answers, the minimal sufficient witnesses, are what we mean by explanations, mechanisms and reasons. These problems usually ask for multiple minimal witnesses, yet standard RL methods may reveal only one solution or redundant ones. We formalize this problem as minimal-witness identification and introduce Minimal-Witness Reinforcement Learning (MWRL). MWRL takes the union of the sets certified by successful proposals sampled from the policy and credits each proposal for the coverage the group union would lose without that proposal. This credit assignment, derived directly from the problem definition, unifies the demands for minimality and recovery of alternatives from a single black-box verifier bit. Under this principle, we derive a value iteration planner that recovers the entire family of witnesses and a policy gradient method that can scale to large language models. Across different experimental settings, MWRL recovers most minimal witnesses, while other methods return redundant supersets or a single witness. By making witness families learnable from verifier feedback, MWRL expands the scope of reinforcement learning beyond single-solution optimization. Our code is available at https://github.com/TSUITUENYUE/MWRL.

通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).title: Robot Learning with Visual Predicted Force
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).authors_text: Haonan Chen, Feiyang Wu, Yuxiang Ma, Mustafa Mete, Pengfei Ye
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).summary: This paper presents a method for force-aware manipulation using visual force prediction from a compliant gripper, eliminating the need for specialized force sensors during deployment.
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).debug_abstract: Force-aware manipulation typically relies on specialized force or tactile sensors. We show that force-aware manipulation can instead be achieved through visual force prediction from the deformation of a compliant Fin Ray gripper. Our approach trains two models. First, we train a visual force estimator on calibration data and use it to annotate task demonstrations with force estimates. Second, we train an action--force proposal policy on these force-augmented demonstrations to jointly generate candidate robot actions and their associated forces. At test time, we sample candidate actions and the forces they are expected to produce, then execute the action whose predicted force is closest to a target from the demonstrations. We evaluate our approach on berry picking, empty-can grasping, in-hand reorientation, and plug insertion. Our results show that visual force prediction can guide inference-time action selection for contact-rich manipulation without requiring force or tactile sensors at deployment.

通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).authors_text: Shibo Jin, Zhiqiu Xu, Yiling Zou, Shangyu Gong, Mayur Naik
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).summary: The paper introduces Environment Duels, a benchmark evaluating LLMs' abilities to create and solve interactive environments, revealing distinct skills and co-evolutionary dynamics among models.
通用机器人、自动化、传感和感知实验室 (GRASP).debug_abstract: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. Each model writes environments, each with a privileged hint, aiming for tasks that capable solvers fail without the hint and pass with it. Across nine frontier LLMs, solving and authoring prove to be distinct skills: the strongest solvers are not the strongest authors, while smaller models learn more from how others played and write the hardest environments and the most useful hints. Beyond the scores, the pairwise interactions form a microcosm of how models affect one another. Head-to-head outcomes are transitive and so yield a stable ranking; independent authors converge on the same designs; and in a reinforcement-learning study with Qwen3.8-27B, the learner's hint lift on an author's environments tracks how much training on those environments improves it on held-out reasoning and agentic benchmarks, whether the environments are its own or another model's. Each of these patterns has a counterpart in how models shape one another outside the duel. By staging these interactions under controlled conditions, Environment Duels offers a window onto how LLMs teach, challenge and learn from one another. Code is available at https://github.com/LLM-Duels/EnvDuels.

Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelli.title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelli.authors_text: Ruotong Liao, Meikel Kokowski, Xiaoxiao Sun, Yongqin Xian, Laura Bravo Sánchez
Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelli.summary: ProactEgoMem introduces a benchmark for evaluating proactive memory in streaming egocentric video, focusing on tasks like information capture, state tracking, and location tracking.
Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelli.debug_abstract: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. 斯坦福-人工智能实验室 (SAIL).debug_abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. 斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).authors_text: Hyunji Alex Nam, Michael Dennis, Natasha Jaques, Minsuk Chang
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).summary: The paper presents TURTLE, an unsupervised approach for evolving scalable, self-tuning benchmarks to enhance AI tool-use capabilities across diverse applications.
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).debug_abstract: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $τ$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.

斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).title: SSIO: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).authors_text: Yuheng Qiu, Yutian Chen, Carlton Cort, Weison Huang, Shibo Zhao
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).summary: The SSIO method enables training inertial odometry models without ground-truth trajectories by using integration self-supervision and pose graph distillation, achieving high accuracy across diverse platforms.
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).debug_abstract: Learning inertial odometry for a new platform usually requires ground-truth trajectories. We show that an inertial odometry model can instead be trained from scratch by a myopic teacher that integrates the IMU over each short window independently, a scheme we call integration self-supervision. Interestingly, although supervised only by short-window velocity changes, the student learns to directly predict velocity, and does so more accurately than its integration teacher. Pose graph distillation then refines the model with sequence-consistent targets from a pose graph over many windows. Training on a new platform therefore no longer requires collecting ground-truth trajectories, but only calibrating the IMU and recording data during normal operation. Across six datasets spanning pedestrians, drones, quadrupeds, and a humanoid, the same recipe with no velocity or position labels trains models that come within 0.07~m/s average velocity error of a same-architecture supervised baseline.

斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).title: FallGown: A Soft Pneumatic Wearable Device for Fall Prevention
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).authors_text: Megan C. Coram, Haoran Lei, Steven H. Collins, Steve B. Cousins, Michelle Baldonado
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).summary: The FallGown is a lightweight, soft pneumatic wearable device designed to prevent falls in older adults, offering support and adaptability while minimizing user burden.
斯坦福-机器人与具身智能实验室 (REAL).debug_abstract: Concerns about falling and potential resulting injuries prevent many older adults from participating in forms of health-improving exercise such as walking, dance, and tai chi. Existing passive devices like walkers require use of the arms for support, and active devices like exoskeletons and robotic frames are often rigid, bulky, and stigmatized, which limits their use. The FallGown is a soft wearable support structure consisting of pressurized pneumatic pouches within a fabric shell; it can support the full weight of a user's body and aims to prevent falls. It is portable (6.9 kg and 0.051 m3 when stored), minimally burdensome (7.24-20.8 N drag force depending on floor type and whether an optional rolling base frame is used), and convenient (less than 2.5 minutes on average to don and less than 0.5 minutes on average to doff). The optional rolling base lowers friction with the floor, but reduces portability and skirt deformation (which can be useful to fit through doors and other tight spaces). Fall prevention testing with a single user revealed a tradeoff between device size and stability against tipping; a skirt with 12 pneumatic pouches and a floor diameter of 1.4 meters with a base frame prevented all falls except in one case with a mechanical failure. On-board pressure sensors can sense the user's weight distribution, providing an opportunity for monitored exercise and adaptive support.

南京大学.title: CoLVR: Enhancing Exploratory Latent Visual Reasoning via Contrastive Optimization
南京大学.authors_text: Ziyang Ding, Linjian Meng, Yiming Wu, Yuhan Li, Yuhao Liu
南京大学.summary: CoLVR enhances exploratory latent visual reasoning in MLLMs through a novel contrastive optimization framework, achieving significant performance improvements in various benchmarks.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Due to the potential for exploratory reasoning of Latent Visual Reasoning, recent works tend to enable MLLMs (Multimodal Large Language Models) to perform visual reasoning by propagating continuous hidden states instead of decoding intermediate steps into discrete tokens. However, existing works typically rely on hard alignment objectives to force latent representations to match predefined visual features, thereby severely limiting the exploratory of latent reasoning process. To address this problem, we propose CoLVR (Contrastive Optimization for Latent Visual Reasoning). To obtain a more exploratory visual reasoning, CoLVR introduces a latent contrastive training framework. Firstly, CoLVR learns diverse and exploratory representations with a latent contrastive objective guided by angle-based perturbation, which expands the semantic latent space and avoids over-constrained embedding. Then, CoLVR employs a latent trajectory contrastive reward for RL (Reinforcement Learning) post-training to enable fine-grained optimization of latent visual reasoning process and thus fostering diverse reasoning behaviors. Experiments demonstrate that CoLVR significantly enhances the exploratory capability of latent representations, achieving average improvements of 5.83% on VSP and 8.00% on Jigsaw, while also outperforming existing latent models on out of domain benchmarks, with a 3.40% gain on MMStar. The data, codes, and models are released at https://github.com/Oscar-dzy/CoLVR.

南京大学.title: AirPlayground: Benchmarking Aerial Navigation across Diverse Reconstructed Environments
南京大学.authors_text: Rangya Zhang, Yujing Shang, Zhuoyuan Yu, Mingsheng Li, Qingsong Yan
南京大学.summary: AirPlayground is a benchmark for aerial navigation, offering 94 photorealistic environments and extensive flight demonstrations to evaluate and train diverse navigation policies.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large-scale aerial resources provide a foundation for learning navigation across diverse environments. However, existing resources remain limited in providing (1) densely sampled flight demonstrations for learning different policy formulations and (2) broad environment coverage for standardized closed-loop evaluation. To address these limitations, we introduce AirPlayground, a unified benchmark for training and evaluating aerial navigation policies across diverse environments. We first construct 94 photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) environments spanning indoor, urban outdoor, and vegetation settings, with aligned collision geometry. Building on these environments, we develop a scene-adaptive pipeline for automated expert flight collection, yielding 94K demonstrations and 46.5M synchronized observation-state-action samples at 50 Hz. We further provide an extensible API that supports training different policy formulations on this shared corpus and evaluating them under unified protocols in the corresponding environments. We benchmark seven baselines spanning four policy paradigms across three navigation settings in seen and unseen environments, and further examine scaling behavior with ACT. Scaling ACT's training corpus from 5 to 70 scenes raises median success rates on seen and unseen environments from 30.6% and 16.8% to 41.2% and 29.4%, respectively. Through this shared training and evaluation framework, AirPlayground supports analysis of how offline prediction errors relate to closed-loop outcomes. Our analyses highlight the roles of prediction errors, execution protocols, and scene interactions in closed-loop performance.

南京大学.title: Learning What to Remember: Resource-Efficient Self-Improvement for Lifelong Agents
南京大学.authors_text: Guannan Lai, Zi-Yang Bai, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye
南京大学.summary: TokenWorth is a resource-efficient framework that enhances lifelong agents' decision-making by optimizing memory usage based on the relevance and worth of past experiences.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Self-improving agents aim to continuously improve their behavior by learning from experience after deployment. However, accumulating and reusing more experience does not necessarily lead to better decisions, particularly when generation, interaction, and memory resources are jointly constrained. Under such stringent constraints, we find that several existing lifelong-memory methods provide limited benefits over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents. This reveals a fundamental challenge for resource-efficient self-improvement: agents must learn not only which past experiences are relevant, but which are actually worth reusing to improve future decisions. When memory capacity and opportunities for reasoning and recovery are limited, retrieving an ineffective experience can consume scarce resources and hinder downstream execution. To address this challenge, we propose TokenWorth, a lightweight feedback-driven memory adaptation framework that learns query-dependent memory worth from sparse execution feedback. Without updating the backbone model, TokenWorth uses the learned worth to guide both experience retrieval and bounded memory management, enabling the agent to continually adapt how it reuses accumulated experience. Across three LifelongAgentBench environments and both local and API-based deployments, TokenWorth achieves the highest task success rate while using the fewest output tokens among the evaluated methods under the specified resource budgets. These results suggest that effective self-improvement under resource constraints depends not on accumulating more experience, but on learning what is worth remembering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/AIGNLAI/TokenWorth.

南京大学.title: Value-Rectified Distillation for Flow-based Offline Reinforcement Learning
南京大学.authors_text: Ke Jiang, Wen Jiang, Yoshinobu Kawahara, Xiaoyang Tan
南京大学.summary: The paper introduces Value-Rectified Distillation (VRD), a framework that mitigates Out-of-Distribution issues in offline reinforcement learning by decoupling behavioral modes and enhancing high-value action isolation.
南京大学.debug_abstract: We aim to address the problem of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Mode Averaging, a critical problem that emerges when distilling Flow Matching (FM) based behavior policies in offline Reinforcement Learning (RL): When learning over multi-modal datasets, standard distillation inadvertently forces the policy to interpolate across different behavioral modes, causing the generated actions to collapse into invalid, OOD regions. To resolve this, we propose Value-Rectified Distillation (VRD), a novel framework that reformulates offline policy distillation as a value-guided generative trajectory alignment problem. By employing a dynamic coupling mechanism, VRD actively rectifies flow dynamics to explicitly decouple distinct behavioral modes, cleanly isolating high-value actions. Specifically, we instantiate VRD through two complementary algorithms: VRD-Q, which utilizes value-quantile behavior distillation to statistically filter out low-value behaviors, and VRD-R, which reorganizes the latent space to geometrically isolate high-value generative trajectories from the FM-based behavior policy. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that VRD improves existing generative baselines across diverse continuous control and planning tasks on the D4RL, OGBench, and Minari benchmarks, especially over those multi-modal, non-expert datasets.

南京大学.title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
南京大学.authors_text: Jinglin Dai, Jiawan Wang, Ruiqi Hong, Lei Bu
南京大学.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical feedback framework that enhances LLMs' ability to generate executable plans for cyber-physical systems by addressing intent misinterpretation and execution feasibility.
南京大学.debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Kuan Zhang, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yue Su, Xiangnan Wu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The study evaluates continued pre-training for embodied agents across diverse virtual worlds, revealing that data volume, diversity, and model size impact performance and generalization differently.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: SDPose: Exploiting Diffusion Priors for Out-of-Domain and Robust Pose Estimation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Shuang Liang, Jing He, Lejun Liao, Chuanmeizhi Wang, Guo Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: SDPose leverages diffusion model features for robust, cross-domain human pose estimation, achieving competitive performance with efficient fine-tuning on a new COCO-based benchmark.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Pre-trained diffusion models provide rich latent features across U-Net levels and are emerging as powerful vision backbones. While prior works such as Marigold and Lotus repurpose diffusion priors for dense geometric perception tasks such as depth and surface normal estimation, their potential for cross-domain human pose estimation remains largely unexplored. Through a systematic analysis of latent features from different upsampling levels of the Stable Diffusion U-Net, we identify the levels that deliver the strongest robustness and cross-domain generalization for pose estimation. Building on these findings, we propose SDPose, which (i) extracts U-Net features from the selected upsampling blocks, (ii) fuses them with a lightweight feature aggregation module to form a robust representation, and (iii) jointly optimizes keypoint heatmap supervision with an auxiliary latent reconstruction loss to regularize training and preserve the pre-trained generative prior. To evaluate cross-domain generalization and robustness, we construct COCO-OOD, a COCO-based benchmark with four subsets: three style-transferred splits to assess domain shift and one corruption split (noise, weather, digital artifacts, and blur) to test robustness. With data-efficient fine-tuning, SDPose achieves performance comparable to Sapiens on COCO, and establishes the best zero-shot performance on cross-domain datasets.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Kai Zhu, Yintianrun Zhang, Shuwei Jiang, Ruolin Zuo, Yixin Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: CausalAlign enhances ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based video generation models by aligning representations to a 3D foundation model, improving geometric accuracy and performance in mobile manipulation tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: LiveAct introduces a multi-agent video world model that utilizes a Heterogeneous Action Interface for independent control and semantic adaptation of diverse action commands across various tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: FoveaVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by utilizing learned foveation actions to replace wrist cameras, improving manipulation success rates in various tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Wrist cameras provide close-up detail but restrict the view to the end-effector's surroundings. External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Tengda Guo, Jie Leng, Hanlei Li, Yaoyuan Liang, Qingyue Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: CAVE enhances Vision-Language Models' fragmented visual reasoning by optimizing intermediate actions through structured credit assignment, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general multimodal reasoning, yet remain challenged in integrating nonlocal visual information to support semantically underdetermined visual reasoning. We describe this challenge as Fragmented Visual Reasoning. To this end, we propose Credit Assignment for Visual Evidence (CAVE), a structured process-reward method based on GRPO for interleaved visual reasoning. Specifically, CAVE evaluates the contribution of intermediate steps at the action level via three complementary reasoning process signals: belief update, evidence acquisition, and adaptive focus control, thereby guiding the model to optimize each reasoning action and learn more reliable visual reasoning strategies. Meanwhile, we construct TRACER-Bench, which covers four nonlocal and semantically confusable reasoning dimensions and provides key intermediate evidence to supervise reasoning paths. Experiments demonstrate that CAVE substantially improves performance on tasks requiring fragmented visual evidence integration, covering both public benchmarks and our newly introduced TRACER-Bench, while retaining competitive performance on general multimodal evaluations. Further analyses reveal that CAVE effectively improves the visual reasoning capacity and exhibits stronger robustness under longer-range and deeper cross-region dependencies.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xuanfeng Yang, Le Gai, Jiaming Wang, Xuan Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), enhancing student learning by dynamically adjusting teacher supervision based on capability gaps, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Learning from Fleet Experience: Collective Experience Learning Across 96 Robots
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper presents Collective Experience Learning (CEL), enabling 96 robots to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving success rates of 93.3-99.2% in various tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). FERT uses failure contexts to retrieve relevant segments from successful trajectories and prioritizes their recorded actions for supervised updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. Operators provide binary episode-outcome labels and environment resets. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates robot execution, cloud inference and policy optimization despite local interruptions. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Kai Zhu, Yintianrun Zhang, Shuwei Jiang, Ruolin Zuo, Yixin Chen
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: CausalAlign enhances ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based video generation models by aligning representations to a 3D foundation model, improving geometric accuracy and performance in mobile manipulation tasks.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: LiveAct introduces a multi-agent video world model that utilizes a Heterogeneous Action Interface for independent control and semantic adaptation of diverse action commands across various tasks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. 智能技术与系统实验室.title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: FoveaVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by utilizing learned foveation actions to replace wrist cameras, improving manipulation success rates in various tasks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions.
