External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Tengda Guo, Jie Leng, Hanlei Li, Yaoyuan Liang, Qingyue Zhang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: CAVE enhances Vision-Language Models' fragmented visual reasoning by optimizing intermediate actions through structured credit assignment, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general multimodal reasoning, yet remain challenged in integrating nonlocal visual information to support semantically underdetermined visual reasoning. We describe this challenge as Fragmented Visual Reasoning. To this end, we propose Credit Assignment for Visual Evidence (CAVE), a structured process-reward method based on GRPO for interleaved visual reasoning. Specifically, CAVE evaluates the contribution of intermediate steps at the action level via three complementary reasoning process signals: belief update, evidence acquisition, and adaptive focus control, thereby guiding the model to optimize each reasoning action and learn more reliable visual reasoning strategies. Meanwhile, we construct TRACER-Bench, which covers four nonlocal and semantically confusable reasoning dimensions and provides key intermediate evidence to supervise reasoning paths. Experiments demonstrate that CAVE substantially improves performance on tasks requiring fragmented visual evidence integration, covering both public benchmarks and our newly introduced TRACER-Bench, while retaining competitive performance on general multimodal evaluations. Further analyses reveal that CAVE effectively improves the visual reasoning capacity and exhibits stronger robustness under longer-range and deeper cross-region dependencies.

智能技术与系统实验室.title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Xuanfeng Yang, Le Gai, Jiaming Wang, Xuan Zhang
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper introduces Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), enhancing student learning by dynamically adjusting teacher supervision based on capability gaps, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. 智能技术与系统实验室.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: Collective Experience Learning Across 96 Robots
智能技术与系统实验室.authors_text: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan
智能技术与系统实验室.summary: The paper presents Collective Experience Learning (CEL), enabling 96 robots to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving success rates of 93.3-99.2% in various tasks.
智能技术与系统实验室.debug_abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). FERT uses failure contexts to retrieve relevant segments from successful trajectories and prioritizes their recorded actions for supervised updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.

MARS多模态学习实验室.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
MARS多模态学习实验室.authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
MARS多模态学习实验室.summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.
MARS多模态学习实验室.debug_abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...

To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. 智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet

External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Tengda Guo, Jie Leng, Hanlei Li, Yaoyuan Liang, Qingyue Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: CAVE enhances Vision-Language Models' fragmented visual reasoning by optimizing intermediate actions through structured credit assignment, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general multimodal reasoning, yet remain challenged in integrating nonlocal visual information to support semantically underdetermined visual reasoning. We describe this challenge as Fragmented Visual Reasoning. To this end, we propose Credit Assignment for Visual Evidence (CAVE), a structured process-reward method based on GRPO for interleaved visual reasoning. Specifically, CAVE evaluates the contribution of intermediate steps at the action level via three complementary reasoning process signals: belief update, evidence acquisition, and adaptive focus control, thereby guiding the model to optimize each reasoning action and learn more reliable visual reasoning strategies. Meanwhile, we construct TRACER-Bench, which covers four nonlocal and semantically confusable reasoning dimensions and provides key intermediate evidence to supervise reasoning paths. Experiments demonstrate that CAVE substantially improves performance on tasks requiring fragmented visual evidence integration, covering both public benchmarks and our newly introduced TRACER-Bench, while retaining competitive performance on general multimodal evaluations. Further analyses reveal that CAVE effectively improves the visual reasoning capacity and exhibits stronger robustness under longer-range and deeper cross-region dependencies.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Xuanfeng Yang, Le Gai, Jiaming Wang, Xuan Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), enhancing student learning by dynamically adjusting teacher supervision based on capability gaps, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Learning from Fleet Experience: Collective Experience Learning Across 96 Robots
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents Collective Experience Learning (CEL), enabling 96 robots to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving success rates of 93.3-99.2% in various tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.

具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).summary: The paper presents Collective Experience Learning (CEL), enabling 96 robots to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving success rates of 93.3-99.2% in various tasks.
具身视觉与机器人实验室 (EVAR Lab).debug_abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). FERT uses failure contexts to retrieve relevant segments from successful trajectories and prioritizes their recorded actions for supervised updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. Operators provide binary episode-outcome labels and environment resets. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates robot execution, cloud inference and policy optimization despite local interruptions. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Kuan Zhang, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yue Su, Xiangnan Wu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The study evaluates continued pre-training for embodied agents across diverse virtual worlds, revealing that data volume, diversity, and model size impact performance and generalization differently.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: SDPose: Exploiting Diffusion Priors for Out-of-Domain and Robust Pose Estimation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Shuang Liang, Jing He, Lejun Liao, Chuanmeizhi Wang, Guo Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: SDPose leverages diffusion model features for robust, cross-domain human pose estimation, achieving competitive performance with efficient fine-tuning on a new COCO-based benchmark.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Pre-trained diffusion models provide rich latent features across U-Net levels and are emerging as powerful vision backbones. While prior works such as Marigold and Lotus repurpose diffusion priors for dense geometric perception tasks such as depth and surface normal estimation, their potential for cross-domain human pose estimation remains largely unexplored. Through a systematic analysis of latent features from different upsampling levels of the Stable Diffusion U-Net, we identify the levels that deliver the strongest robustness and cross-domain generalization for pose estimation. Building on these findings, we propose SDPose, which (i) extracts U-Net features from the selected upsampling blocks, (ii) fuses them with a lightweight feature aggregation module to form a robust representation, and (iii) jointly optimizes keypoint heatmap supervision with an auxiliary latent reconstruction loss to regularize training and preserve the pre-trained generative prior. To evaluate cross-domain generalization and robustness, we construct COCO-OOD, a COCO-based benchmark with four subsets: three style-transferred splits to assess domain shift and one corruption split (noise, weather, digital artifacts, and blur) to test robustness. With data-efficient fine-tuning, SDPose achieves performance comparable to Sapiens on COCO, and establishes the best zero-shot performance on cross-domain datasets.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: CausalAlign: Causal Alignment of Video Generation Models for Consistent Ego-Motion
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Kai Zhu, Yintianrun Zhang, Shuwei Jiang, Ruolin Zuo, Yixin Chen
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: CausalAlign enhances ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based video generation models by aligning representations to a 3D foundation model, improving geometric accuracy and performance in mobile manipulation tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Diffusion-based video generation models (VGMs) can produce visually plausible videos, yet their camera ego-motion often drifts over long horizons. Camera ego-motion determines how the viewpoint changes between frames and is essential for maintaining consistent geometry and trajectories. To address this problem, we propose CausalAlign, a causal alignment framework with two components. First, we diagnose how precise ego motion is represented, used, and retained within VGMs using linear probes and causal interventions, revealing a rise-and-fall pattern during denoising. Second, we strengthen ego-motion state in VGM by aligning the representations at the identified layers to a 3D foundation model through delta-token space. This space encodes the changes between consecutive frames, allowing the alignment to focus on ego-motion dynamics rather than static scene content. With Wan2.2 fine-tuned on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, CausalAlign can largely improve motion accuracy, geometric consistency, and temporal smoothness, while preserving visual quality. For example, it improves geometric consistency by more than 20% relative to the base model. Moreover, with the fine-tuned VGM, CausalAlign improves the success rate of world action models (WAMs) by 10 points on mobile manipulation tasks of RoboCasa365 benchmark. Overall, CausalAlign improves ego-motion consistency in diffusion-based VGMs and yields noticeable gains in embodied models.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: LiveAct introduces a multi-agent video world model that utilizes a Heterogeneous Action Interface for independent control and semantic adaptation of diverse action commands across various tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: FoveaVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by utilizing learned foveation actions to replace wrist cameras, improving manipulation success rates in various tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Wrist cameras provide close-up detail but restrict the view to the end-effector's surroundings. External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: CAVE: A Structured Credit Assignment Approach for Fragmented Visual Evidence Reasoning
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Tengda Guo, Jie Leng, Hanlei Li, Yaoyuan Liang, Qingyue Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: CAVE enhances Vision-Language Models' fragmented visual reasoning by optimizing intermediate actions through structured credit assignment, improving performance on complex reasoning tasks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general multimodal reasoning, yet remain challenged in integrating nonlocal visual information to support semantically underdetermined visual reasoning. We describe this challenge as Fragmented Visual Reasoning. To this end, we propose Credit Assignment for Visual Evidence (CAVE), a structured process-reward method based on GRPO for interleaved visual reasoning. Specifically, CAVE evaluates the contribution of intermediate steps at the action level via three complementary reasoning process signals: belief update, evidence acquisition, and adaptive focus control, thereby guiding the model to optimize each reasoning action and learn more reliable visual reasoning strategies. Meanwhile, we construct TRACER-Bench, which covers four nonlocal and semantically confusable reasoning dimensions and provides key intermediate evidence to supervise reasoning paths. Experiments demonstrate that CAVE substantially improves performance on tasks requiring fragmented visual evidence integration, covering both public benchmarks and our newly introduced TRACER-Bench, while retaining competitive performance on general multimodal evaluations. Further analyses reveal that CAVE effectively improves the visual reasoning capacity and exhibits stronger robustness under longer-range and deeper cross-region dependencies.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Beyond Policy Discrepancy: Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xuanfeng Yang, Le Gai, Jiaming Wang, Xuan Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), enhancing student learning by dynamically adjusting teacher supervision based on capability gaps, outperforming existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) integrates domain specialists into a shared student, but determining how strongly each teacher should supervise remains challenging. Existing discrepancy-based allocation can assign strong supervision even when the student already matches or exceeds the teacher's task performance, since behavioral mismatch does not necessarily imply a remaining capability deficit. We propose Capability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (CA-MOPD), which combines specialist merging with capability-guided allocation to account for what the student has already learned. CA-MOPD first merges reinforcement-learning specialists into a strong student initialization, then uses verifier-estimated teacher--student capability gaps to adjust domain-level distillation strength. Supervision decreases as capability gaps close and increases when estimated student capability regresses, while dense token-level guidance remains provided by the teachers. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and instruction following, CA-MOPD achieves an average score of 32.22, outperforming naive MOPD, Open-MOPD, and the merged initialization by 0.86, 0.83, and 0.74 points, respectively. Controlled comparisons further support the benefits of merged initialization and capability-gap guidance under matched training budgets.

机器人控制实验室.authors_text: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan
机器人控制实验室.summary: The paper presents Collective Experience Learning (CEL), enabling 96 robots to enhance policy reliability by sharing execution experiences, achieving success rates of 93.3-99.2% in various tasks.
机器人控制实验室.debug_abstract: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: SafeDojo: Safe Reinforcement Learning for VLA via Interactive World Model
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Kai Tang, Peidong Jia, Zhong Chu, Jiajun Cao, Jixian Wu
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: SafeDojo introduces a model-based safe reinforcement learning framework that enhances vision-language-action policies using an interactive world model, achieving improved safety and task success rates in real-world applications.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Safe control is a prerequisite for real-world embodied intelligence, for which safe reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, existing safe reinforcement learning methods either require costly real-world exploration or depend on hand-crafted safety functions. Jun MA老师实验室.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...

Jun MA老师实验室.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: LiveAct introduces a multi-agent video world model that utilizes a Heterogeneous Action Interface for independent control and semantic adaptation of diverse action commands across various tasks.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: Cartender: Verifiable Language-Conditioned Driving by Learning the Drives Not Taken
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Zhiwen Chen, Benjin Zhu, Yan Xie, Jun Ma
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: Cartender enhances language-conditioned driving by learning from unchosen actions, improving instruction adherence and reducing infeasible executions through counterfactual branching and scene-language compatibility scoring.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Every driving scene is logged once, but driving is one-to-many: the scene determines which behaviors are feasible, while an instruction selects among them. A log records only the action taken, leaving no direct supervision for alternative feasible actions or instructions the scene cannot support. Consequently, a policy that ignores language and one that follows it without regard to scene constraints can fit the same data. We present Cartender, which learns from the drives not taken. Counterfactual Branching constructs matched and mismatched instruction-action pairs from real recordings without a simulator: a vision-language model proposes alternative futures and their selecting instructions, while unsupported instructions provide negative labels. A learned scene-language compatibility score regulates language conditioning in trajectory generation, and a reward-trained language residual re-ranks generated candidates over a scene-based score. The branches are used for training; instruction following is evaluated by swapping instructions under identical recorded inputs and measuring behavior rather than agreement with generated targets. On WOD-E2E, the best of four proposals achieves an RFS of 8.642 across 3,603 feasible instruction conditions. Across 8,974 admitted proposals, mean RFS is 8.203 versus 7.906 for matched logged trajectories, and 67% score higher than their logged counterpart. Compared with matched-only imitation using the same backbone, Cartender improves same-scene paired instruction success from 23.67% to 57.00% and RFS from 6.32 to 7.10; its gate reduces infeasible-instruction execution from 53.36% to 14.18%.

机器人研究所.authors_text: Kai Tang, Peidong Jia, Zhong Chu, Jiajun Cao, Jixian Wu
机器人研究所.summary: SafeDojo introduces a model-based safe reinforcement learning framework that enhances vision-language-action policies using an interactive world model, achieving improved safety and task success rates in real-world applications.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Safe control is a prerequisite for real-world embodied intelligence, for which safe reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising paradigm. 机器人研究所.title: VeriCalib: Verifiable Target-Based LiDAR-Camera Calibration
机器人研究所.authors_text: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Feiyi Chen, Shengli Ren, Shiyang Chen
机器人研究所.summary: VeriCalib introduces a verifiable framework for target-based LiDAR-camera calibration, enhancing reliability by assessing extrinsic estimation through structured covariance and directional precision checks.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. Consequently, the fitted residual can reveal neither an inconsistency between the observations and the model nor whether the estimated extrinsic is reliable in every direction. Accordingly, we assess the calibration through a structured covariance that jointly propagates the uncertainty of the camera and LiDAR board features with a known-geometry prior, and estimate its scale as a variance component from the residuals. On this covariance, we decouple rotation and translation to resolve the precision along each direction and guide data collection toward the weakest one. Since this precision presumes consistent observations, we further develop within-view and cross-view checks that examine the internal residual and the rigid discrepancy between observations, respectively, with thresholds that hold their significance level under an unknown noise level. We also extend the minimal detectable bias to the extrinsic to bound the smallest detectable fault along each direction. These criteria form a calibration state that indicates whether to accept the result or how to collect the data...

机器人研究所.title: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
机器人研究所.authors_text: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi
机器人研究所.summary: LiveAct introduces a multi-agent video world model that utilizes a Heterogeneous Action Interface for independent control and semantic adaptation of diverse action commands across various tasks.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.

机器人研究所.title: Cartender: Verifiable Language-Conditioned Driving by Learning the Drives Not Taken
机器人研究所.authors_text: Zhiwen Chen, Benjin Zhu, Yan Xie, Jun Ma
机器人研究所.summary: Cartender enhances language-conditioned driving by learning from unchosen actions, improving instruction adherence and reducing infeasible executions through counterfactual branching and scene-language compatibility scoring.
机器人研究所.debug_abstract: Every driving scene is logged once, but driving is one-to-many: the scene determines which behaviors are feasible, while an instruction selects among them. A log records only the action taken, leaving no direct supervision for alternative feasible actions or instructions the scene cannot support. Consequently, a policy that ignores language and one that follows it without regard to scene constraints can fit the same data. We present Cartender, which learns from the drives not taken. Counterfactual Branching constructs matched and mismatched instruction-action pairs from real recordings without a simulator: a vision-language model proposes alternative futures and their selecting instructions, while unsupported instructions provide negative labels. A learned scene-language compatibility score regulates language conditioning in trajectory generation, and a reward-trained language residual re-ranks generated candidates over a scene-based score. The branches are used for training; instruction following is evaluated by swapping instructions under identical recorded inputs and measuring behavior rather than agreement with generated targets. On WOD-E2E, the best of four proposals achieves an RFS of 8.642 across 3,603 feasible instruction conditions. Across 8,974 admitted proposals, mean RFS is 8.203 versus 7.906 for matched logged trajectories, and 67% score higher than their logged counterpart. Compared with matched-only imitation using the same backbone, Cartender improves same-scene paired instruction success from 23.67% to 57.00% and RFS from 6.32 to 7.10; its gate reduces infeasible-instruction execution from 53.36% to 14.18%.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Michael Chen, Hong Chul Nam, Xi Deng, Anima Anandkumar
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: The paper presents Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that efficiently learns noise-aware value fields for robust planning in diverse environments, outperforming existing methods in speed and success rate.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. Building on an established screened-Poisson formulation of stochastic optimal control, we address two challenges: specifying boundary conditions that support navigation across varying geometries and efficiently computing fields with reliable gradients. Zero-Dirichlet obstacle boundaries terminate sampled paths at walls, weakening the goal signal along long routes and making it harder to estimate reliably. We instead impose reflecting Neumann conditions on obstacles and a Dirichlet condition at the goal, allowing sampled paths to continue exploring free space until they reach the target. To solve the resulting PDE without a configuration-space mesh, we extend a Monte Carlo (MC) solver, Walk on Stars (WoSt), to higher dimensions. However, local MC fluctuations can reverse estimated gradient directions and cause planning failures, making direct planning require costly sampling. PUN amortizes this computation by learning geometry-to-field mappings from noisy, partially converged Monte Carlo labels, avoiding expensive convergence for every training example. At inference, test-time scaling uses bounded local search guided by the predicted global field. We evaluate PUN on planning tasks across dimensions. Across four noise levels, PUN matches or outperforms all compared planners, achieving 95-100% success on the 4D replanning benchmark while maintaining the lowest runtime. At the highest tested noise level in 4D, PUN achieves 10.7-60.6% relative gains in success rate over other methods while running 3.29-32.15 times faster.

Rajpurkar Lab.title: Robot Learning with Visual Predicted Force
Rajpurkar Lab.authors_text: Haonan Chen, Feiyang Wu, Yuxiang Ma, Mustafa Mete, Pengfei Ye
Rajpurkar Lab.summary: This paper presents a method for force-aware manipulation using visual force prediction from a compliant gripper, eliminating the need for specialized force sensors during deployment.
Rajpurkar Lab.debug_abstract: Force-aware manipulation typically relies on specialized force or tactile sensors. We show that force-aware manipulation can instead be achieved through visual force prediction from the deformation of a compliant Fin Ray gripper. Our approach trains two models. First, we train a visual force estimator on calibration data and use it to annotate task demonstrations with force estimates. Second, we train an action--force proposal policy on these force-augmented demonstrations to jointly generate candidate robot actions and their associated forces. At test time, we sample candidate actions and the forces they are expected to produce, then execute the action whose predicted force is closest to a target from the demonstrations. We evaluate our approach on berry picking, empty-can grasping, in-hand reorientation, and plug insertion. Our results show that visual force prediction can guide inference-time action selection for contact-rich manipulation without requiring force or tactile sensors at deployment.

Rajpurkar Lab.title: AI-driven Prices for Externalities and Sustainability in Production Markets
Rajpurkar Lab.authors_text: Panayiotis Danassis, Aris Filos-Ratsikas, Haipeng Chen, Milind Tambe, Boi Faltings
Rajpurkar Lab.summary: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning agent that optimizes market prices to address negative externalities and enhance sustainability in production markets.
Rajpurkar Lab.debug_abstract: Traditional competitive markets do not account for negative externalities; indirect costs that some participants impose on others, such as the cost of over-appropriating a common-pool resource (which diminishes future stock, and thus harvest, for everyone). Quantifying appropriate interventions to market prices has proven to be quite challenging. We propose a practical approach to computing market prices and allocations via a deep reinforcement learning policymaker agent, operating in an environment of other learning agents. Our policymaker allows us to tune the prices with regard to diverse objectives such as sustainability and resource wastefulness, fairness, buyers' and sellers' welfare, etc. As a highlight of our findings, our policymaker is significantly more successful in maintaining resource sustainability, compared to the market equilibrium outcome, in scarce resource environments.

Rajpurkar Lab.title: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
Rajpurkar Lab.authors_text: Kaichen Zhou, Yuzhen Chen, Hannah Yao, Chonghe Jiang, Rao Fu
Rajpurkar Lab.summary: T-WLA integrates visual memory with tactile feedback to enhance contact-rich manipulation, achieving significant improvements in hand-motion prediction and real-world task success rates.
Rajpurkar Lab.debug_abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.

Rajpurkar Lab.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
Rajpurkar Lab.authors_text: Vahid Hosseinzadeh, T. Anderson Keller, Michael Puthawala
Rajpurkar Lab.summary: The paper introduces Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM (MELSTM), enhancing sequence modeling by treating motion as a gauge symmetry, outperforming traditional models in various tasks.
Rajpurkar Lab.debug_abstract: Objects move, cameras pan, and weather drifts with the wind: much of what changes in sequential data is motion. Motion changes where things are, not what they are, and is therefore a symmetry of the data. Yet standard recurrent networks are not equivariant to it: their memory stays put while the input moves on. Flow equivariant recurrent networks first brought this symmetry into sequence models, for motions of constant velocity, or flows, by enumerating a bank of velocities. We extend this idea in three directions: from simple recurrent networks to convolutional LSTMs, from flows to motions whose velocity changes in time, and from enumerating velocities to estimating them. Treating a sequence as a field over time, we show that motion becomes a gauge symmetry: a global symmetry made local in time. Built on this view, our motion equivariant convolutional LSTM (MELSTM) uses its velocity model as the gauge field and is provably equivariant to every motion. Across future-frame prediction, classification of digits visible only through their motion, and action recognition under camera shake, MELSTM outperforms a convolutional LSTM and its flow equivariant counterpart with the same number of parameters: it is more accurate, generalizes to longer horizons and to unseen motions, and carries a fraction of the flow equivariant model's state.

CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.authors_text: William Huang, David Li, Xiang 'Anthony' Chen, Xun Qian, Nels Numan
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.summary: GenXR-Bench is a pioneering benchmark for evaluating coding agents in interactive XR development, assessing their performance across diverse tasks and identifying key failure areas.
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.debug_abstract: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.

CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.title: FracEvent: Event-Camera Simulation via Fractional-Relaxation Pixel Dynamics
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.authors_text: Langyi Chen, Chuanzhi Xu, Haoxian Zhou, Pengfei Ye, Ziyu Luo
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.summary: FracEvent is a novel event-camera simulator that utilizes fractional-relaxation dynamics to enhance event generation, achieving superior performance in image reconstruction and optical flow estimation.
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.debug_abstract: Event cameras asynchronously report brightness changes with microsecond-level temporal resolution, but real event data remain difficult to collect at scale because specialized sensors, careful synchronization, and task-specific annotations are required. Event-camera simulation is therefore important to event-based vision tasks. Most practical simulators build on contrast-threshold event generation, some with additional filtering, stochastic noise, or calibrated sensor parameters. While effective, such formulations can simplify the temporal structure produced by a pixel's recent response history. We introduce FracEvent, a physics-inspired sensor-side simulator with compact fractional-relaxation voltage dynamics. Given a log-intensity trajectory, FracEvent combines fast and slow response modes, emits ON/OFF events by localizing threshold crossings on the continuous voltage trajectory, and updates the event reference while retaining the mode states. This retained state links residual response to later event timing. We evaluate FracEvent through direct event-stream comparison and downstream transfer on image reconstruction and optical flow estimation. Across multiple datasets, FracEvent achieves leading results on multiple metrics in both evaluations, showing its practical value for event-camera simulation. Project page: https://bonaparte233.github.io/FracEvent/

CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.authors_text: Kaichen Zhou, Yuzhen Chen, Hannah Yao, Chonghe Jiang, Rao Fu
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.summary: T-WLA integrates visual memory with tactile feedback to enhance contact-rich manipulation, achieving significant improvements in hand-motion prediction and real-world task success rates.
CSAIL Embodied Intelligence Labs.debug_abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.

Quest for Intelligence.title: GenXR-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive XR Development
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: William Huang, David Li, Xiang 'Anthony' Chen, Xun Qian, Nels Numan
Quest for Intelligence.summary: GenXR-Bench is a pioneering benchmark for evaluating coding agents in interactive XR development, assessing their performance across diverse tasks and identifying key failure areas.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: Coding agents are rapidly advancing from single-file generation to long-horizon repository-scale engineering, yet the evaluation of their capabilities to author interactive extended reality (XR) applications remains an open challenge. Unlike traditional software, XR applications operate within dynamic 3D physical environments where runtime robustness depends jointly on continuous user motion, spatial input, and environmental sensing. We introduce GenXR-Bench, the first benchmark for the end-to-end evaluation of coding agents in XR software development. GenXR-Bench contains 112 expert-authored tasks spanning 24 feature implementations, 21 bug repairs, and 67 application generation tasks. Held-out tests combine scripted and adaptive interactions with programmatic and visual assertions to evaluate core functionality and runtime behavior. GenXR-Bench's testing suite achieves 96.5% accuracy against blinded expert judgments of 124 candidate applications executed on consumer XR hardware. Evaluating 10 models on GenXR-Bench, we find that the strongest configuration achieves only 50.9% overall Pass@1. Failure analysis identifies recurring misunderstandings in asynchronous sensor lifecycles, physical grounding, and embodied interaction semantics. GenXR-Bench establishes a reproducible testbed for evaluating coding agents in the interactive and physically situated conditions of spatial computing.

Quest for Intelligence.title: Robot Learning with Visual Predicted Force
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Haonan Chen, Feiyang Wu, Yuxiang Ma, Mustafa Mete, Pengfei Ye
Quest for Intelligence.summary: This paper presents a method for force-aware manipulation using visual force prediction from a compliant gripper, eliminating the need for specialized force sensors during deployment.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: Force-aware manipulation typically relies on specialized force or tactile sensors. We show that force-aware manipulation can instead be achieved through visual force prediction from the deformation of a compliant Fin Ray gripper. Our approach trains two models. First, we train a visual force estimator on calibration data and use it to annotate task demonstrations with force estimates. Second, we train an action--force proposal policy on these force-augmented demonstrations to jointly generate candidate robot actions and their associated forces. At test time, we sample candidate actions and the forces they are expected to produce, then execute the action whose predicted force is closest to a target from the demonstrations. We evaluate our approach on berry picking, empty-can grasping, in-hand reorientation, and plug insertion. Our results show that visual force prediction can guide inference-time action selection for contact-rich manipulation without requiring force or tactile sensors at deployment.

Quest for Intelligence.title: FracEvent: Event-Camera Simulation via Fractional-Relaxation Pixel Dynamics
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Langyi Chen, Chuanzhi Xu, Haoxian Zhou, Pengfei Ye, Ziyu Luo
Quest for Intelligence.summary: FracEvent is a novel event-camera simulator that utilizes fractional-relaxation dynamics to enhance event generation, achieving superior performance in image reconstruction and optical flow estimation.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: Event cameras asynchronously report brightness changes with microsecond-level temporal resolution, but real event data remain difficult to collect at scale because specialized sensors, careful synchronization, and task-specific annotations are required. Event-camera simulation is therefore important to event-based vision tasks. Most practical simulators build on contrast-threshold event generation, some with additional filtering, stochastic noise, or calibrated sensor parameters. While effective, such formulations can simplify the temporal structure produced by a pixel's recent response history. We introduce FracEvent, a physics-inspired sensor-side simulator with compact fractional-relaxation voltage dynamics. Given a log-intensity trajectory, FracEvent combines fast and slow response modes, emits ON/OFF events by localizing threshold crossings on the continuous voltage trajectory, and updates the event reference while retaining the mode states. This retained state links residual response to later event timing. We evaluate FracEvent through direct event-stream comparison and downstream transfer on image reconstruction and optical flow estimation. Across multiple datasets, FracEvent achieves leading results on multiple metrics in both evaluations, showing its practical value for event-camera simulation. Project page: https://bonaparte233.github.io/FracEvent/

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Samuel Foo Enze, Manthan Patel, Fan Yang, Linus Kramer, Pascal Roth
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: RangeNav is a compact LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained on synthetic data, enhancing robot navigation in complex environments through improved representation learning and performance metrics.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Jumping in Lunar Gravity
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Levin Müller, Oliver Fischer, Marco Trentini, Yusuke Tanaka, Marco Hutter
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: This paper presents a multistage reinforcement learning approach for a legged robot's effective point-to-point jumping in lunar gravity, demonstrating successful simulation and hardware execution.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Legged robots can extend planetary exploration to rugged and discontinuous terrain that is inaccessible to conventional rovers. In lunar gravity, jumping further expands this mobility by enabling robots to cross obstacles and gaps that cannot be traversed by walking alone. We present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that produces a single end-to-end control policy for commanded point-to-point jumping under lunar gravity. The resulting policy has a simple architecture and relies exclusively on mission-compatible onboard sensing, making its deployment on a real lunar mission plausible. In simulation, the learned policy performs accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size. We analyze the torque and power demands of lunar jumping and characterize performance degradation under extreme outlier events, including control-update freezes of up to \SI{1}{s} during flight. Hardware transfer demonstrates that the policy can successfully execute a vertical jump under lunar-gravity offloading. Furthermore, the measured torque and power profiles are consistent with the simulation results and remain within the robot's hardware limits.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: LitePT: Lighter Yet Stronger Point Transformer
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Yuanwen Yue, Damien Robert, Jianyuan Wang, Sunghwan Hong, Jan Dirk Wegner
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: LitePT optimizes 3D point cloud processing by combining early convolution layers for geometry and deep attention layers for semantics, achieving significant efficiency improvements.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Modern neural architectures for 3D point cloud processing contain both convolutional layers and attention blocks, but the best way to assemble them remains unclear. We analyse the role of different computational blocks in 3D point cloud networks and find an intuitive behaviour: convolution is adequate to extract low-level geometry at high-resolution in early layers, where attention is expensive without bringing any benefits; attention captures high-level semantics and context in low-resolution, deep layers more efficiently, where convolution inflates the parameter count. Guided by this design principle, we propose a new, improved 3D point cloud backbone that employs convolutions in early stages and switches to attention for deeper layers. To avoid the loss of spatial layout information when discarding redundant convolution layers, we introduce a novel, parameter-free 3D positional encoding, PointROPE. The resulting LitePT model has $3.6\times$ fewer parameters, runs $2\times$ faster, and uses $2\times$ less memory than the state-of-the-art Point Transformer V3, but nonetheless matches or outperforms it on a range of tasks and datasets. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/prs-eth/LitePT.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Matthew Strong, Ankush K. Dhawan, Julien Poffet, Giuse Pham, Jinho So
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R) transforms a single human RGB video into thousands of robot demonstrations by semantically aligning objects, enhancing robot learning efficiency.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.

Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.title: The Stepwise Informativeness Assumption: When Do Entropy Dynamics Track Reasoning Correctness in LLMs?
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.authors_text: Mar Gonzàlez I Català, Haitz Sáez de Ocáriz Borde, George D. Montañez, Pietro Liò
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.summary: This paper introduces the Stepwise Informativeness Assumption, analyzing how entropy dynamics in LLMs relate to reasoning correctness across various benchmarks and training regimes.
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.debug_abstract: Recent work uses entropy-based signals at multiple representation levels to study reasoning in large language models, but the field remains largely empirical. From a theoretical perspective, reductions in model uncertainty do not necessarily reflect progress toward correctness. In this work, we characterize when such alignment can be expected through the Stepwise Informativeness Assumption (SIA), which requires entropy-reducing reasoning-prefix extensions increase the probability assigned to valid answers in expectation. We show that next-token prediction can transfer answer-relevant information from training data to the model, but does not, by itself, guarantee alignment with correctness. Instead, we propose that this alignment depends on how the training regime couples reasoning traces to correct answers. Furthermore, we hypothesize observable signatures of this phenomenon and characterize its expected failure regimes. We empirically investigate how entropy dynamics relate to correctness across four reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, ARC, SVAMP, MATH) and diverse open-weight language models spanning base, instruction-tuned, and RL-trained regimes. Our results show that entropy-correctness alignment strengthens with post-training but can weaken when task difficulty exceeds model capabilities.

Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.title: inr2action: Encoding Robot Episodes as Neural Implicit Representations for Recall and Action
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.authors_text: Leann Alhashishi, Christos Margadji, Sebastian William Pattinson
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.summary: The paper introduces a parameter-space memory framework that encodes robot episodes as fixed-size weight deltas, enabling efficient long-horizon operation and scalable memory management.
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.debug_abstract: Long-horizon robotic operation requires memory that scales with essential information rather than execution time. We present a parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object. A neural implicit representation is fitted to episode video from a shared, meta-learned initialization; the resulting weight delta constitutes the memory. Crucially, this delta remains a fixed size regardless of whether the episode spans a hundred or a hundred thousand frames. A learned projector maps the weight delta into token embeddings, conditioning a language model for question answering and a decoder for joint command regression, without frame retrieval at query time. On RoboMME, the language model exceeds chance across all question types, and the decoder achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.51. Replacing the delta with matched noise drops performance by 11.4 points, while random-origin weights are non-decodable, proving the meta-learned initialization is essential for embedding episode content. By representing individual experiences as fixed-size weight deltas in a common parameter space, this approach decouples memory cost from time horizon and provides a basis for scalable streaming memory.
